Subject: [Urgent] Intermittent 502s and TCP resets to private deployment

Olga / Redwood team,

We started seeing intermittent 502s from our integration with the Private deployment you manage in our VPC around 09:30 UTC. Symptoms: short spikes of timeouts on API requests (~1-3 minutes), many client retries, and our load balancer reporting a lot of TCP RSTs. Our infra team grabbed a quick tcpdump during an incident window and attached a small pcap (fintech_pcap_excerpt.tar.gz).

Initial observations from our firewall: elevated SYN-RETRY counts and session table pressure. We also included a snapshot of the Palo Alto state (pa-fw-state-snapshot.log). We suspect NAT/session exhaustion or connection-tracking limits between the customer NAT and your edge nodes.

Can someone from your side confirm whether you saw connection failures or any recent config changes? This is impacting production traffic.

Thanks,
Doug Weber
Head of Platform — FintechCo

Subject: Re: [Urgent] Intermittent 502s and TCP resets to private deployment

Thanks for the context — I pulled the edge host conntrack counters and firewall integration logs. Quick summary of findings: 

- conntrack_count peaked at ~98% of nf_conntrack_max on the edge host during the incident windows (see attached conntrack-counters-before-after.txt).
- The Palo Alto snapshot shows a burst of half-open sessions (SYN_RETRY) and many short-lived flows that never complete the 3-way handshake.
- There are clients that rapidly open many concurrent connections (retries + exponential backoff behavior causing retried SYNs).

Potential root causes (in order):
1) Upstream NAT or edge firewall running out of ephemeral ports / conntrack entries (translation failures).
2) A misbehaving client (or load balancer) generating many connection attempts without backing off — amplifying conntrack usage.
3) MTU/fragmentation causing TCP handshake issues (less likely given SYN counts but worth checking).

Immediate mitigations we recommend: 
- If acceptable, we will increase nf_conntrack_max on the edge hosts by 50% as a temporary measure and monitor. Commands: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` (value depends on host memory).
- Add a short conntrack timeout for SYN_SENT/SYN_RECV to age half-open entries faster: `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_syn_sent` and friends.
- On the customer's firewall/NAT: review ephemeral port pool sizing and any PAT timeouts.
- Implement an edge-level rate-limit for SYNs per source IP for ~60s to defeat rapid fanout clients.

I'll stand up a short runbook and can apply the temporary sysctl change if Monica/@ops+fintech give the go-ahead. If this persists, we'll schedule a coordinated maintenance to tune both sides and deploy a permanent rate-limiting rule on the Private edge.

-Marcu s Lin

Principal Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
